sections.title: Basic Concept of Word Formation and Logical Sequence
sections.content: In this topic, words must either be arranged in the correct order or new words must be formed from a given word. Step 1: Identify the type of question (Sequence, Dictionary Order, or Word Formation). Step 2: Apply the appropriate rule. Step 3: Compare with the options and choose the correct answer.

sections.title: Logical Sequence of Words
sections.content: In this type of question, 4–5 words must be arranged in a natural or logical order. Step 1: Understand the meaning of all words. Step 2: Identify the relationship between them (size, process, time, or value). Step 3: Start with the smallest or earliest stage. Step 4: Form the correct sequence. Example: Seed → Plant → Tree → Fruit.

sections.title: Dictionary Order (Alphabetical Order)
sections.content: In dictionary order, words must be arranged according to the alphabetical order of the English alphabet. Step 1: Compare the first letters. Step 2: If the first letters are the same, compare the second letters. Step 3: Continue comparing the next letters in the same way. Step 4: Form the correct alphabetical sequence. Example: Apple, Banana, Mango, Zebra.

sections.title: Word Formation
sections.content: In word formation, a new word must be formed using the letters of a given root word. Step 1: List the letters of the root word. Step 2: Check how many times each letter appears. Step 3: Match the letters in the option with the available letters. Step 4: If any letter appears more times than available or is missing, the word cannot be formed. Example: From 'ENVIRONMENT', the word 'MINT' can be formed, but 'MENTOR' cannot be formed if the required letters are not available.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Arranging words without understanding their meanings. 2. Ignoring the second letter during alphabetical comparison. 3. Not checking the number of letters in word formation. 4. Guessing answers in a hurry.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In logical sequence, identify the natural order. In dictionary order, compare letters step by step. In word formation, check both the availability and the frequency of letters. Practice improves speed and accuracy.

tricks.title: Meaning First Method
tricks.explanation: In logical sequence questions, first understand the meaning of all words.

tricks.title: Process Order Identification
tricks.explanation: If the words represent a process, arrange them from the beginning to the end.

tricks.title: Alphabet Step Check
tricks.explanation: In dictionary order, first compare the first letters.
tricks.example: Ant, Bat, Cat is the correct order.

tricks.title: Second Letter Rule
tricks.explanation: If the first letters are the same, check the second letters.
tricks.example: Ball, Bell, Bill — the order is determined by 'a', 'e', 'i'.

tricks.title: Letter Count Trick
tricks.explanation: In word formation, check the number of times each letter appears.
tricks.example: From APPLE, 'PEAL' can be formed but 'APPLY' cannot.

tricks.title: Missing Letter Check
tricks.explanation: If an option contains a letter not present in the root word, the word cannot be formed.
tricks.example: From TEAM, 'MEAT' can be formed but 'MATEY' cannot.

tricks.title: Check the Longest Word First
tricks.explanation: Longer words require more letters, so they can be verified quickly in word formation.

tricks.title: Visual Comparison Method
tricks.explanation: In alphabetical order, compare words letter by letter.
tricks.example: Care, Card, Cart — the order is determined by 'd' and 'e'.
